operator_request: Resolve WP-FF-015's failed wreq transport-candidate decision with a two-engine direction, explicitly approving shipped reqwest 0.13.4 with rustls 0.23.42 and native ring 0.17.14 under narrow Ferric-owned controls while wreq remains non-shipped and disabled; use distinct-lens subagents to adversarially review and harden the implementation.

current_primary_sources.evidence: Official release history identifies reqwest 0.13.4 as the current stable release.

The official builder exposes explicit DNS resolver injection, address overrides, redirect policy, no-proxy mode, timeouts, per-host idle-pool controls, TLS backend selection, and decompression disable controls; defaults include automatic redirects, system proxy discovery through the default feature set, no total timeout, and no bounded global in-flight admission.
The rustls feature selects aws-lc-rs, while rustls-no-provider permits an explicit provider and default features also enable system-proxy behavior.
Rustls documents maintained aws-lc-rs and ring providers and supports constructing a ClientConfig with an explicitly supplied provider.
The all-Rust provider is alpha, incomplete, and explicitly warns against production use.
The browser-emulation v6 candidate remains a release candidate and retains the native BoringSSL surface adjudicated by WP-FF-015.

inspected_implementation_evidence: A repository-local disposable Cargo metadata resolution proved reqwest 0.13.4 with its rustls feature selects aws-lc-rs 1.17.3, aws-lc-sys 0.43.0, ring 0.17.14, cmake, and native build/link surfaces.

A second repository-local disposable Cargo metadata resolution proved reqwest 0.13.4 with rustls-no-provider plus rustls 0.23.42 ring selects the narrower ring 0.17.14 native link/build surface without AWS-LC or CMake.

Direct inspection of the locked ring 0.17.14 crate proved that its packaged Windows build consumes bundled C source plus pregenerated NASM object files from the crate; FF-DEC-002 must expose and govern that exact packaged-object boundary rather than claiming a source-only Windows build.

Locked Cargo metadata and source inspection proved rustls-no-provider selects rustls-platform-verifier 0.7.0; its Windows verifier uses native FFI, so the package must remain explicitly governed even though Ferric's provider-bound ClientConfig bypasses platform trust selection at runtime.
The exact graph inspection ran under .fforager-artifacts and the canonical cleanup gate subsequently verified items=0.
selected_approach: Create FF-DEC-002 as the exact Operator-approved shipped native dependency decision for future fforager-net use of reqwest 0.13.4, rustls 0.23.42, and ring 0.17.14.
Require reqwest default features off, rustls-no-provider, a provider-bound ring ClientConfig, exact webpki-roots 1.0.9, and only the reviewed HTTP/2 and streaming feature surface.

Authorize ring's packaged pregenerated Windows assembly objects only for exact locked ring 0.17.14, with Cargo.lock and cached archive checksums, full extracted source-tree digest, exact features, recursive content-inventory digest, reachability, and native-link validation; do not generalize that allowance to other prebuilt artifacts.

Record rustls-platform-verifier 0.7.0 as an exact selected native-runtime package, validate its Cargo.lock/archive/full-source identity, Windows FFI source and empty feature set, and prove the ordinary runtime path bypasses it through reqwest's preconfigured TLS boundary.

Pin the complete ordinary root-reachable package identity, selected-feature, and edge closure under separate FF-DEC-002 authority so build policy alone cannot self-authorize an unknown no-links FFI dependency.

Keep Ferric authoritative for destination admission, DNS/SSRF receipts, redirects, cookies, proxies, pool partitioning, concurrency, byte/decompression bounds, timeouts, retries, cancellation, and diagnostics.
Retain FF-DEC-001 only for the existing non-shipped WP-FF-015 evidence; wreq remains forbidden from product, packaging, release, and runtime paths.
Represent fingerprint-required requests as a stable typed browser-transport-required refusal until a separate fingerprint transport closes its blockers and receives a new Operator decision.
Extend the architecture validator so product-native exceptions are explicit, exact, mechanically distinct from prerequisite-only exceptions, and mutation-tested.
rejected_options: Reqwest's normal rustls feature because it silently selects the broader aws-lc-rs/aws-lc-sys and CMake surface in addition to ring.
Rustls RustCrypto because its current provider is alpha, incomplete, and explicitly not production-ready.
Promoting wreq because WP-FF-015 retained unresolved wire-parity, DNS/SSRF, pool, cancellation, and cross-platform blockers and the Operator explicitly kept it non-shipped.
Forking wreq or hand-building browser fingerprints because Ferric would inherit a security-critical, continuously changing browser-wire maintenance burden.
Adding Chromium, curl-impersonate, libcurl, Python, yt-dlp, or another runtime/native path because the Operator did not authorize them and their packaging/lifecycle surface is larger.

Building the complete Phase 1 downloader in this packet because the request resolves the transport decision and Phase 1 additionally requires storage, archive, watcher, diagnostics, launcher, and staged-runtime closure.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: The rustls label hides native crypto or feature drift.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Pin all three direct versions, disable defaults, enumerate exact features/native links/build packages, and make architecture mutations for AWS-LC, native-tls, default features, version drift, and extra consumers fail.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Ring's crates.io Windows build silently consumes packaged pregenerated assembly objects while governance claims no prebuilt inputs.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Expose a ring-specific packaged-object authority bit and canonical object-inventory digest, retain the general prebuilt-binary prohibition, verify exact ring identity/features/source markers/object bytes through the locked package, and mutation-test authority or digest drift.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: The rustls-no-provider label hides rustls-platform-verifier's selected Windows FFI dependency.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Govern exact rustls-platform-verifier 0.7.0 as a native-runtime package, validate its selected feature/source surface, bind reqwest to a Ferric-built rustls ClientConfig and root store, and report the selected-but-bypassed package explicitly.
Require no_proxy, no automatic redirects, no cookie store, no automatic decompression, no dependency retry authority, explicit deadlines, and Ferric-owned admission before any future production I/O.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Ordinary HTTPS success is mislabeled browser compatibility.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Make TLS and HTTP/2 fingerprint requirements return a typed browser-transport-required result before network execution and retain mandatory corpus blockers.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Client reuse crosses security contexts or bypasses global limits.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Require immutable Ferric pool keys and separately constructed clients per compatible partition; resource admission remains outside reqwest and must bound global and per-origin in-flight work.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: The decision packet is mistaken for shipped capability.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Keep the exact prerequisite zero-progress ceiling and require the future fforager-net consumer to re-prove the decision through FF-GATE-RUNTIME-001.

basis.validation_plan: Resolve and lock the exact reqwest/rustls/ring graph in the non-shipped transport proof package; extend canonical native-exception validation to distinguish product-authorized and prerequisite-only decisions; add declaration-preserving mutations for consumer, runtime class, product-use flag, versions, features, AWS-LC/default-feature drift, native links, ring packaged-object authority, wreq product reachability, and browser-required refusal; run transport, xtask, architecture, runtime-ceiling, deep/PR as triggered, and secret gates; dispatch distinct transport-security, resource-lifecycle, and dependency/proof-integrity reviewers; remediate confirmed findings with public-boundary regressions and rerun the complete matrix.

assumptions: The Operator's exact approval authorizes the named shipped dependency surface but not the complete Phase 1 runtime slice.
The future production consumer is the accepted fforager-net package from design Section 9.
Canonical proof remains offline; current external source checks establish dependency selection context but do not become runtime proof.
non_goals: Shipped downloader or fforager CLI implementation.
Wreq product promotion or browser-fingerprint compatibility.
Global Phase 1 readiness or product-progress claims.
Delegating Ferric security, resource, retry, cookie, redirect, or diagnostics authority to reqwest.

attack_lenses: native dependency and additive Cargo feature escape
browser-fingerprint downgrade or false capability success
structural graph checks mislabeled behavioral proof
minimum_controls: At least three distinct-lens subagent reviews after implementation.
At least two implementation-independent checks beyond the implementer's command list.
Concrete counterfactuals for product-native authorization and browser-required refusal.
Boundary and negative probes for policy defaults, consumer/runtime drift, native-link drift, wreq reachability, and false PASS.
Every confirmed finding becomes a public-boundary regression before closure.
